result:
The proposed answer $\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\approx 0.618$ is too small. A simple space-barrier construction forces $c\ge 1/\sqrt2\approx 0.707$.

**Construction.** Let $V_1, V_2, V_3$ be the parts, each of size $n$. Choose $A_1\subseteq V_1$ with $|A_1|=an$ and $B_1\subseteq V_2$ with $|B_1|=bn$. Let $H$ consist of all triples $(x,y,z)\in V_1\times V_2\times V_3$ with $x\in A_1$ or $y\in B_1$.

**No perfect matching when $a+b<1$.** Each vertex of $V_1\setminus A_1$ lies only in triples whose $V_2$-vertex is in $B_1$. These $(1-a)n$ vertices need distinct $V_2$-partners, all in $B_1$, so $(1-a)n\le bn$, i.e. $a+b\ge 1$. Hence for $a+b<1$ there is no perfect matching.

**Link spectral radii.**
- $x\in A_1$: the link is the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$, so $\rho=n$.
- $x\in V_1\setminus A_1$: the link is $K_{B_1,V_3}$, so $\rho=\sqrt{bn\cdot n}=\sqrt b\,n$.
- $y\in V_2\setminus B_1$: the link is $K_{A_1,V_3}$, so $\rho=\sqrt a\,n$.
- $y\in B_1$: the link contains $K_{V_1,V_3}$, so $\rho=n$.
- $z\in V_3$: the link is $K_{n,n}$ minus the complete bipartite graph on $(V_1\setminus A_1)\times(V_2\setminus B_1)$. It contains $K_{A_1,V_2}$, so $\rho\ge\sqrt a\,n$. It also contains $K_{V_1,B_1}$, so $\rho\ge\sqrt b\,n$. Hence $\rho\ge\max(\sqrt a,\sqrt b)\,n\ge\min(\sqrt a,\sqrt b)\,n$.

So every vertex has $\rho\ge\min(\sqrt a,\sqrt b)\,n$. Taking $a=b=\tfrac12-\varepsilon$ (so $a+b<1$) gives $\rho\ge(1/\sqrt2-O(\varepsilon))\,n$ for every vertex, yet no perfect matching exists.

Therefore any valid $c$ must satisfy $c\ge 1/\sqrt2$. The proposed value $\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}<\frac1{\sqrt2}$ fails: this construction violates the claimed theorem for any $\alpha$ small. The parity construction in the proposed solution does not justify its upper bound either. The intended constant appears to be $1/\sqrt2$.

VERDICT: REJECT
